content:
Kai: Heads-up — saw a ~20% regression on A100 for seq=1024 after the autotune refactor.
Sarah: which commit? link?
Kai: commit 9f3a2d, changed kernel selector to prefer tile-optimized kernels for sm80. quick logs attached below.
Miguel: are we sure it's the selector and not a side-effect (batching heuristics)?
perf-bot: benchmark summary: a100/seq1024/batch8 p95 78ms -> 94ms (+20%) ; l4/seq1024/batch8 p95 120ms -> 115ms (-4%)
Kai: repro command I ran: `./bench --model redwood-v1 --device a100 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kernel-autotune on`
Kai: nvprof snippet:
```
GPU kernel time (warp-opt): 42.3ms
KV memcpy/pipeline stall: 15.1ms
Batch occupancy: 38%
```

Sarah: that memcpy stall looks suspect. on A10/L4 the selector picked compute-light kernels which keep KV copy smaller?
Miguel: correct — compute-light uses an interleaved kv layout that reduces pmem traffic for small batches. tile-optimized warp kernels trade more registers for throughput and cause larger intermediates.
Kai: observed KV cache thrash on A10 with the warp kernel too at small seqs (<256) — p95 spikes.
Sarah: current autotune state key is (device_family, model). we need to include seqlen bucket. right now single entry causes bad cross-seqlen choices.
Miguel: proposed change: autotune key -> (device_family, model, seq_bucket) where seq_bucket in {<=256, 257-512, 513-1024, >1024}. also add kv_friendly flag for kernels.
Kai: +1. also add a cheap heuristic: prefer kv_friendly when batch*seqlen < 2048 or when observed kv memcpy stall > 5ms.
Sarah: can we make this a non-destructive rollout? plan: pin current autotune state in prod for 24h, push seqlen-keying to canary, run sweep across [L4,T4,A10] vs [A100,H100]. if p95 > baseline+10% rollback.
perf-bot: canary plan queued: sweep devices: [L4,T4,A10,A100,H100], seqs: [128,256,512,1024,2048], batches: [1,4,8]. expected run time ~6h.
Miguel: I'll add a preset JSON for the seqlen-aware autotune; name it `seqbucket-device-fallback` and include an explicit fallback policy: on p95 regression >10% for 30m route to alternate kernel family.
Kai: sample preset snippet:
```json
{
  "preset_name": "seqbucket-device-fallback",
  "autotune_key": ["device_family","model","seq_bucket"],
  "kv_friendly_threshold": 2048,
  "fallback_policy": {"p95_delta_pct": 10, "window_min": 1800}
}
```
Sarah: include an integration test in perf-suite: synthetic prompt set that stresses KV reuse + chat-like prefixes. keep it lightweight.
Miguel: opened PR #862 with the preset + autotune change + unit tests, added a smoke perf job.
Kai: added runtime guard: if new autotune table causes any production route p95 to exceed baseline+10% we auto-pin old table and emit alert.
perf-bot: canary started: eng-runtime-canary-7 ; will report back in ~6h.
Sophie: tagging release windows — scheduling 1h maintenance tomorrow 10:00 UTC in case we need a quick rollback.
Kai: FYI I'll run an nvprof + kernel flamegraph on the A100 repro and dump artifacts to /artifacts/perf/2183021111 for follow-up.
Sarah: thanks — great triage. next steps: land PR #862 after canary ✅, merge preset, update runtime metrics dashboard (per-route seqlen buckets).
Miguel: noted. filing follow-up issue: #489 "autotune: support seq-bucketed keys + kv-friendly kernel tagging".
Kai: :thumbsup:
Sarah: closing loop once canary finishes.
